# Current release · Keystone Polygon experience R6 · 2026-11-14

index.html is a ten-chapter story in 29 scenes about one real Eagle County, Colorado parcel (220531300003, 4.235 ha, a historical screening candidate). Direct route ?chapter=ID with optional &step=ID. Chapters: polygon, living, engine, spillover, measured, clock, forecast, windows, obligation, next.

A Keystone Polygon is a parcel whose condition and position shape what happens to people and places well beyond its boundary, a name it earns only when an active function, a pathway across the boundary and a recipient who would feel its loss have each been shown. No Colorado parcel is validated as one. Keystone function, pathway, recipient, rights, payer and financial return are all unestablished for this parcel.

The story shows the parcel as a node in a dependency graph that runs from land through living communities, ecosystem processes and pathways to recipients, consequences and an obligation. Each scene that presents evidence is tagged Computed, Observed, Tested, Published elsewhere, Illustrative or Pending. Published ecology comes from other places and is unmeasured on the parcel. Terrain results describe the shape of the surface and carry no measured flow. North Inlet, East Inlet and the Glenwood station are separate cases with no traced delivery from the parcel. No atmospheric transport.

The framework generates machine-readable records for agents (a dependency graph, an evidence passport, a claim register, a reference register, a data inventory and a release manifest with integrity hashes). They are held by Graph of Life and shared on request. The core methods are withheld.

passport.html is the candidate file. review.html is the historical monitoring budget review. evidence.html and legacy.html are earlier releases kept for the record.

Contact: jg@graphoflife.com, https://biome-translator.emergent.host/.
